summary.oneLiner: AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited is the Indian arm of a global, science-led, patient-focused biopharmaceutical group, marketing innovator specialist medicines across Oncology, Biopharmaceuticals and Rare Disease.

currentContext.strengths: Innovator, patent-protected specialist portfolio backed by the global AstraZeneca group's asset pipeline across oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, respiratory and immunology|Regulatory throughput: 20 product approvals (including label expansions) secured since FY24-25, with 13 approvals in FY25-26 alone|Oncology leadership - described as the Company's most powerful growth engine in India, propelling it into the top 2 oncology players by revenue|Brand durability after loss of exclusivity: Brilinta remains market leader growing at double digit despite LOE in 2019 and entry of close to 40 generics; Lynparza retains market leadership by value share with over 16 biosimilar entrants; Forxiga is among the top 5 brands of Dapagliflozin by value despite 600+ dapagliflozin brands|First-to-market specialist launches - Soliris, India's first anti-complement therapy, and Lokelma, one of the best launches of 2025 by 1st month sales value|Fastest-growing among top companies by revenue in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market in FY 2025-26, growing faster than the top 25 companies and gaining 2 spots to rank #37|Robust clinical operations and evidence-generation capability used to accelerate regulatory milestones in India|Asset-light India model - distribution and marketing led, with manufacturing decommissioned and product supply sourced under long-standing group formulation, packaging and distribution agreements
currentContext.strategies: Focus the India portfolio on Oncology, Cardiovascular, Renal, Metabolism and Respiratory, alongside recent expansion into Rare Diseases|Operate sales and marketing through three business verticals - Biopharmaceuticals Business Unit, Oncology Business Unit and Rare Disease Unit (the latter launched in 2023)|Grow through innovation: introduce new innovative products and secure label / indication expansions to deepen and broaden the existing therapy-area portfolio|Tap the group's asset pipeline to bring life-changing medicines in oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, respiratory and immunology to Indian patients at the earliest, subject to feasibility and regulatory approvals|Leverage robust clinical operations and evidence-generation capabilities to accelerate regulatory milestones in India|Continue to prioritise investments in the Company's focus disease areas, in line with its strategy|Run an asset-light India model - the Company is engaged in distribution and marketing of pharmaceutical products and co-ordinates clinical trial services with an overseas group company, its manufacturing operations having been decommissioned during the year under review|The Company maintains a Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, published on its website; the annual-report text provided sets out the policy's existence rather than a numeric payout philosophy. Governance of remuneration and appointments runs through a formal Nomination and Remuneration Policy covering Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Executives, supported by a vigil mechanism / whistle-blowing policy with direct access to the Audit Committee Chairperson in exceptional cases. On the deployment side the model is deliberately asset-light: no capital investment was made in energy conservation equipment because the factory is undergoing the closure process, and the Company confirms there are no materially significant related party transactions with Promoters, Directors, KMP or Senior Management that may have a potential conflict of interest, with all related-party dealings during FY 2025-26 in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis.|Ambition Zero Carbon - a $1bn global programme investing in reducing GHG emissions across the research, development, manufacture and supply of medicines|88% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions (from sites and fleet) achieved since 2015 while more than doubling revenue, with continued progress targeted|Tackling Scope 3 (value chain) emissions, which represent approximately 98% of the total footprint, through product innovation including transition to the next-generation propellant, supplier engagement, sustainable transport (shifting from air to sea freight) and responsible business travel|2030 targets focused on water stewardship and circularity across sites, complemented by governance and metrics to track performance and scale investments|Nature action: sustainable sourcing and circular resource use to prevent land use change, deforestation and exploitation of natural resources|Pollution minimisation: tracking of the waste circularity rate and recognised industry leadership in managing pharmaceuticals in the environment (PIE)|Nature restoration through global programmes including AZ Forest, working with stakeholders such as indigenous peoples and local communities|Sustainability strategy built on action on climate and nature, health equity and health systems resilience, delivered in collaboration with governments, health systems, patient groups, academia and NGOs|Board-level oversight of sustainability risk: ESG-related risks are explicitly within the Risk Management Committee's risk-identification framework|BRSR reported on a standalone basis with Limited Assurance on BRSR Core Indicators by KPMG Assurance and Consulting Services LLP|Women represent 83.33% of the Board of Directors and 66.7% of Key Management Personnel|Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, anchored on the published Code of Ethics
currentContext.expansion: The Company has no manufacturing capex or capacity-addition programme in this report - its manufacturing operations were decommissioned during the year under review, leaving an India model built on distribution and marketing of pharmaceutical products plus co-ordination of clinical trial services with an overseas group company. Expansion is therefore portfolio-led rather than plant-led: sales and marketing are organised around three verticals (Biopharmaceuticals Business Unit, Oncology Business Unit and the Rare Disease Unit launched in 2023), and growth comes from new molecule introductions and label / indication expansions. The Company secured 20 product approvals including label expansions since FY24-25, with 13 within FY25-26 alone, adding Datverzo in Oncology (unresectable or metastatic breast cancer with relevant mutations) and securing indication extensions across lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction and other tumour types; separately the Board's report notes 11 regulatory approvals for medicines and indications during the year. Capability building beyond the medicine continued through AI-led lung cancer detection, diagnostic capability building, clinical education, Rare Disease advocacy and wider health system partnerships. The remaining site-level capital decision is closure-related: no capital investment was made in energy conservation equipment because the factory is undergoing the closure process.

risks.risk: Loss of the India manufacturing footprint following factory closure
risks.note: The BRSR records a single national site at which manufacturing activities were ceased during the year under review, leaving the entity dependent on group supply for its products and removing in-country production flexibility.

risks.risk: Workforce disruption and elevated attrition from the factory closure
risks.note: All permanent workers left during the year on account of redundancies from the factory closure, and permanent-employee turnover remains a disclosed watch-item across the last three years - a retention and knowledge-continuity risk for a specialist-selling organisation.

risks.risk: Concentration on a single business activity and a narrow customer set
risks.note: The entity's main activity is marketing and trading of pharmaceutical products, sold pan-India to a customer base of distributors, hospitals and Government institutions, with international sales limited to one country (Nepal) - leaving little diversification if that channel or activity is disrupted.

risks.risk: Dependence on a single holding company within the AstraZeneca group
risks.note: AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals AB is disclosed as the Holding Company and the reporting boundary is standalone; product supply, pricing and portfolio choices therefore sit largely with the group rather than with the listed entity.

risks.risk: Product quality and customer complaint exposure
risks.note: Complaints received under the responsible-business-conduct principles from customers mainly pertain to Product Quality Complaints in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, a recurring quality/pharmacovigilance watch-item for a marketing-and-distribution entity.

risks.risk: Climate transition and value-chain (Scope 3) emissions exposure
risks.note: Scope 3 emissions represent approximately 98% of the total footprint and come primarily from purchased goods and services, capital goods, distribution and product use - so decarbonisation depends on suppliers and logistics the Company does not directly control.

risks.risk: Nature, water and pollution dependencies across the value chain
risks.note: Natural resources are described as fundamental to the discovery, development and manufacture of medicines; the Company manages sustainable sourcing, water and circular resource use, pollution minimisation and pharmaceuticals in the environment (PIE) against 2030 site targets.

The Managing Director and two Non-Executive Directors ceased office during FY 2025-26, with consequential turnover in the chairs and membership of the Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders' Relationship and Risk Management Committees.

risks.risk: Enterprise risk categories formally identified by the Board
risks.note: The Risk Management Committee's mandate covers financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability (particularly ESG-related), information and cyber security risks, with a business continuity plan and a policy reviewed at least once in two years; the Committee met twice during the financial year.
